flashcard_questions.a: The process of fertile land turning into desert over time.
A semi-arid region bordering the southern edge of the Sahara.

flashcard_questions.q: What share of the Sahara can be used for farming?
How much rain falls in the Sahara each year?
How many people does Morocco's Noor Power Plant supply with electricity?
How much profit did Moroccan phosphate mining make in 2018?
How much does tourism generate for Morocco each year?
Why does over-cultivation lead to desertification?
flashcard_questions.a: Soil nutrients are exhausted, leaving barren land open to erosion.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does overgrazing lead to desertification?
flashcard_questions.a: Animals eat vegetation faster than it regrows, leaving the ground exposed.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main physical cause of desertification?
Which single outcome do all the causes of desertification share?
How does the Upesi stove slow desertification?
flashcard_questions.a: Its clay oven holds heat, so far less wood is needed for cooking.

flashcard_questions.q: What are bunds in the Sahel?
flashcard_questions.a: Low stone walls laid along slopes to slow rainwater and trap soil.

flashcard_questions.q: How much farmland does Niger lose to desertification each year?
How long will the Great Green Wall belt of trees stretch?

notes: 15 cards: 3 term-to-definition (desertification, Sahel, bunds), 7 case-study-to-fact with one figure each (2% farmland, 250 mm rainfall, 1 million supplied by Noor, £6 billion phosphate, £9 billion tourism, 250,000 hectares in Niger, 7,775 km Great Green Wall), 4 cause-to-consequence (over-cultivation, overgrazing, climate change, shared soil erosion outcome), 1 strategy-to-example (the Upesi stove). Dropped Nouakchott and the 25%-sand-dunes figure so the deck is not top-heavy with Sahara statistics.
